source.title: parseRegexLiteral() rejects valid d and v regex flags and silently returns the whole literal as the pattern

labels.name: status:in-linear
labels.description: Issue or PR is now in Linear

source.body:
### Bug Description

`parseRegexLiteral()` only recognises a slash-delimited regex literal when all trailing flags come from the allowlist `[gimusy]*`. That is the ES2018 set; `d` (hasIndices, ES2022) and `v` (unicodeSets, ES2024) are missing.

When either flag is present the literal is not recognised at all, and the function falls into its "not a literal" branch — returning the **entire input**, slashes and flags included, as the pattern source. The user gets a silently different regex with no error anywhere.

### To Reproduce

1. In any field that accepts a regex literal, enter `/foo/d`.
2. `parseRegexLiteral('/foo/d')` returns `{ source: '/foo/d', flags: '' }`, i.e. it matches the literal text `/foo/d` rather than `foo`.

Expected: `{ source: 'foo', flags: 'd' }`.

The same happens for `/foo/v` and combined flags such as `/foo/gidv`.

### Why this matters

The repo requires Node >= 24 and V8 has supported `d` since Node 16 and `v` since Node 20, so nothing in the runtime prevents these flags. `v` is the modern replacement for the legacy `u` flag and is what makes set notation like `[\p{L}\p{N}]--\p{White_Space}` usable.

The same stale `[gimsuy]` character class also appears in `packages/@n8n/workflow-sdk/src/workflow-builder/string-utils.ts`, so this looks like drift rather than a deliberate restriction.

### Related

Fix proposed in #43021, with regression tests for `d`, `v`, combined flags and `ignoreCase` on top of `v`.
